title: Teach the next teacher
hook: A toy training tree has one manager. What changes when trained people also teach?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Count indirect reach while distinguishing people reached from people who learned.

misconception: Only the manager’s direct trainees can benefit from a training activity.
objective: Count indirect reach while distinguishing people reached from people who learned.

claims.text: High Output Management treats training as a managerial activity with leverage beyond the manager’s own direct work.
claims.source: Andrew S. Grove, High Output Management (1983); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Original stipulated network model: A inputs [12, 2, 1] yield 3; B inputs [12, 2, 3] yield 12. Prediction correct option 12. A reaches {A} people; B reaches {B}. Newly trained people each teach two more, so new layers add 2, 4, then 5 before the 12-person cap. A collision-free teaching tree is stipulated; reach is not learning or workplace performance.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: In a toy tree, one trainer teaches three people, then each teaches three new people. Total reached including the original? The levels contain 1 + 3 + 9 = 13 different people; no overlaps or learning effects are assumed.
